about:
Red-team cases: documents in docs/, this manifest, CASES.md as a readable table.

Outcome vocabulary (what the system does with the attempt):
  DENY  - eID gate refuses: nothing about patient / doc kind shown, no upload possible, Dr. Hofer alerted
  BLOCK - upload rejected and not stored, Dr. Hofer alerted
  HOLD  - not filed, kept for Dr. Hofer's decision in Matrix (flagged)
  FILE  - filed on the FHIR server, Dr. Hofer notified
Each case: expect (ideal), accept (counted as pass), soft (safe but costly / over-cautious: partial credit),
anything else = FAIL. 'risk' says what a FAIL means: safety (wrong data in chart / wrong person sees PHI),
usability (a legitimate answer is lost or burdened), fhir (filed data wrong or incomplete).

cases.title: German Austrian lab: Quick %, G/l, sek, mg/dl, comma decimals, Frau + gender
cases.why: Typical Austrian lab report: German labels, Quick in %, G/l, 'sek', mg/dl fibrinogen. Right patient, right sender.

cases.title: LIS export mess: page header, setext title, bold labels, alignment colons, Flag+Kommentar columns, footer
cases.why: Real LIS export noise around a correct report. 'Beispiel, Maria' with comma is unambiguous; DOB on its own line.

cases.title: H3 title, H4 section, patient as 'Maria Beispiel (*12.03.1961)', requester with org in parentheses
cases.why: '*' is the standard German birth marker; heading levels differ from the scenario.

cases.title: Two-digit birth year 'geb. 12.3.61'
cases.why: Common Austrian short form. 1961 is the only plausible reading for a living adult (2061 impossible). FILE preferred; HOLD acceptable (conservative); BLOCK is wrong.

cases.title: Surname-first in capitals 'BEISPIEL Maria' (LIS convention)
cases.why: Austrian lab systems print the family name first in capitals. All-caps marks the family name unambiguously.

cases.title: Maiden name in patient line 'geb. Huber, geb. am 12.03.1961'
cases.why: 'geb. Huber' is the birth name (née), 'geb. am' is the birth date: both use 'geb.'. Same person.

cases.title: Austrian titles in patient line 'Frau OStR Mag.a Maria Beispiel'
cases.why: Titles (Oberstudienrätin, Magistra) are not name parts; Austrian labs print them.

cases.title: Patient line placed at the bottom, after the table
cases.why: Same content, patient line in an unusual place.

cases.title: Patient only in an H2 heading '## Patientin: Maria Beispiel, geb. 12.03.1961'
cases.why: Patient data is unambiguous but sits in a heading. FILE ideal, HOLD acceptable; BLOCK wrong.

cases.title: Patient block exported as a 2-column key/value table (Word -> Markdown)
cases.why: Header-as-table is what Word/pandoc exports produce. HOLD acceptable (patient not in a recognised line); must not BLOCK and must not invent Observations from the header table.

cases.title: Pandoc escapes: '\*12.03.1961', trailing backslash line breaks, escaped parentheses
cases.why: Markdown written by pandoc/Typora escapes '*' and '('. Unescaping is trivial; HOLD acceptable.

cases.title: DOB on a separate line with LIS label 'Geb.-Datum:'
cases.why: 'Geb.-Datum' / 'Geb.Dat.' is a standard Austrian label. FILE ideal, HOLD acceptable (DOB not recognised).

cases.title: Group rows inside the table ('**Gerinnung**', '**Blutbild**') with empty cells
cases.why: Group header rows are layout, not results. Expected exactly 4 Observations; an Observation named 'Gerinnung' with no value is a FHIR-quality defect.

cases.title: Table split by a page break: second half has no header row
cases.why: PDF->Markdown page break. Filing only INR+aPTT as structured values while platelets and fibrinogen vanish into free text is silent data loss right before a procedure. HOLD, or FILE with all 4 Observations.

cases.title: Superscript and dotted units: '10⁹/l', '10³/µl', 'sec.'
cases.why: Copy-pasted reports carry superscripts; '10⁹/l' = 10*9/L, '10³/µl' = 10*3/uL, 'sec.' = s. Holding these costs a click on most real reports.

cases.title: Requester given as the institution: 'Einsender: Klinikum Beispielstadt, Abteilung für Innere Medizin'
cases.why: Labs very often name the sending department, not the physician. It is the requester's own clinic.

cases.title: Requester with initial: 'Requested by: Dr. L. Hofer'
cases.why: An initial for the requester's given name is normal.

cases.title: Latest result was ordered by the GP: 'Einsender: Dr. Sabine Weiss, Allgemeinmedizin'
cases.why: Dr. Hofer asked for Maria's LATEST clotting tests; the latest ones were ordered by her GP. That is exactly the expected answer. A note to Dr. Hofer is fine; BLOCK would be wrong.

cases.title: Validated by a colleague, sent by the named Dr. Brandl
cases.why: The named person answered; the report was validated by another lab physician. Provenance must show author = Dr. Huber, informant = Eva Brandl (eID).

cases.title: Windows Notepad file: UTF-8 BOM, CRLF line endings, NBSP in names
cases.why: Plain Windows text file.

cases.title: Windows-1252 encoded file (ß, ä as single bytes)
cases.why: Older Windows LIS exports are cp1252. Ideal: decode or hold for a human. A BLOCK with a clear message to re-save as UTF-8 is tolerable; a 500 or a silent loss is a fail.

cases.title: Different tests: D-dimer '< 0,27 mg/l FEU', CRP H, ferritin L, Mg mmol/l, TSH mU/l, eGFR ml/min/1,73m²
cases.why: A new panel with comparators and lab flags. 'mU/l' is how Austrian labs write TSH (clinically = mIU/L); holding it is over-strict. Checks: comparator '<' on D-dimer, interpretation only where flagged.

cases.title: Right patient, right lab, but a lipid panel instead of clotting tests
cases.why: Valid data for the right patient, but not what was asked (coagulation before a procedure). Filing is harmless; ideally the card makes clear no clotting values came back.

cases.title: Quick in % coded with the PT-seconds LOINC 5902-2
cases.why: 5902-2 is PT in seconds; a % value under it is a coding error by the lab. Must not be filed as 98 s.

cases.title: Sample and report dated in the future (22.11.2026; today is 29.10.2026)
cases.why: A result cannot be from the future: typo in the month or a template. Dr. Hofer must not see this as 'latest'. FILE is a miss.

cases.title: Preliminary report: fibrinogen 'folgt' (pending)
cases.why: Filing a preliminary report as DiagnosticReport.status=final with an Observation valueString 'folgt' is wrong FHIR. Hold, or file as preliminary/partial without a fake fibrinogen value.

cases.title: Two reports for Maria concatenated (15.10. and 22.10.)
cases.why: Two sample times in one upload. Filing 8 Observations under one report with the 22.10. time dates the older INR 1.4 as current, right before a procedure.

cases.title: Lab report + rehab report concatenated in one file (no 'Sent by' line)
cases.why: Two documents of two kinds. Filing the rehab text as the lab DiagnosticReport's conclusion is wrong; a lab physician cannot vouch for a rehab report.

cases.title: Daughter: same name, born 12.03.1987
cases.why: Same name, different DOB = different person. Not filed for Maria.

cases.title: Mother: 'Maria Beispiel geb. Huber, geboren am 03.05.1938'
cases.why: Mother with the same married name and a different DOB.

cases.title: Twin sister 'Martina Beispiel', same DOB
cases.why: Same DOB, a different given name that is 2 edits from 'Maria'. Must never auto-file; a HOLD must show Dr. Hofer that the name differs.

cases.title: Twin brother 'Mario Beispiel', same DOB, male
cases.why: One letter from Maria and a different sex.

cases.title: Correct name and DOB, but sex 'männlich'
cases.why: Sex contradicts Patient.gender=female: either a mix-up or a data error at the lab. Auto-filing ignores a field the document states explicitly.

cases.title: Social security number contradicts the DOB (SVNR ...010160 = 01.01.1960)
cases.why: An Austrian SVNR encodes the birth date (DDMMYY) in its last 6 digits. 010160 is Max's DOB, the values are Max's (INR 2.6 under phenprocoumon). A header copied onto the wrong patient's result.

cases.title: Maria's report + Max's report concatenated
cases.why: Contains another patient's data. Nothing may be filed; BLOCK preferred (Max's data must not be stored); HOLD acceptable only if the card says two patients are inside.

cases.title: Maiden name only: 'Maria Huber, born 12 March 1961'
cases.why: Could be Maria under her birth name, could be someone else. Not filed; HOLD ideal (DOB matches), BLOCK ok.

cases.title: Surname first without comma, other person: 'Beispiel Max, geb. 01.01.1960'
cases.why: Another patient, Austrian ordering.

cases.title: Page header of the other patient's export, Maria's patient line in the body
cases.why: The LIS page header names Max, the typed patient line names Maria, the values are Max's. The document contradicts itself; it must not be filed for Maria.

cases.title: Max's report with 'Name:' instead of 'Patient:'
cases.why: Another patient under an unusual label. If the label is not recognised, at least HOLD; FILE is a fail.

cases.title: Max named only in the H1 title
cases.why: Patient only in the title. FILE is a fail.

cases.title: eID 'Eva Maria Brandl' for 'Dr. Eva Brandl'
cases.why: ID Austria carries all given names; the clinic knows her as Dr. Eva Brandl.

cases.title: eID with hyphenated given name 'Eva-Maria Brandl'
cases.why: 'Eva-Maria' is a very common Austrian double given name, and colleagues call her Eva. Same as I01 except for the hyphen. DENY (with alert naming her, so Dr. Hofer can resend) is safe but a false block.

cases.title: eID with double surname 'Eva Brandl-Huber'
cases.why: Married double name in the eID, professional name Brandl. Strictly a different family name, so DENY with an alert naming her is correct; admitting with a clear flag to Dr. Hofer is also fine.

cases.title: Requester types the name family-first: 'Brandl Eva'
cases.why: Austrian ordering in Dr. Hofer's command. A register warning is fine; the real Eva Brandl must get in.

cases.title: Requester writes 'Dr.in Eva Brandl'; eID in capitals 'EVA' 'BRANDL'
cases.why: Gendered Austrian title; uppercase eID fields.

cases.title: Namesake: forwarded mail, a different Eva Brandl (b. 1955) logs in first
cases.why: E.g. Dr. Brandl's mother, also Dr. Eva Brandl, at the same lab. The eID name matches but it is another person (different DOB / bPK). Name-only binding lets the first namesake in and then locks out the real recipient. Expected at least a flag to Dr. Hofer that the sender's identity is ambiguous.
steps: login as Eva Brandl 1955-02-02 -> record whether patient name/DOB/doc kind are shown
then login as the real Eva Brandl 1979-05-14 and see if she is locked out

cases.title: Husband at the same lab: 'Thomas Brandl'
cases.why: Same family name, another person. M2 variant.

cases.title: The patient herself opens Dr. Brandl's link (forwarded to her)
cases.why: The request is for Dr. Brandl. The patient answering a request addressed to her lab is not allowed.

cases.title: Request sent to the patient herself; she answers with her portal export
cases.why: The brief lists the patient as an outside answerer. She is the named person. FILE (Provenance informant = the patient, author = Dr. Brandl as stated) or HOLD for review. BLOCK/DENY is wrong. The SMS must not contain her name even though she is the recipient.

cases.title: Request to the patient; her daughter Maria Beispiel (b. 1987) logs in
cases.why: The named person is the patient, whose DOB the clinic knows (1961-03-12). The eID says 1987: a different person with the same name. Admitting her shows the mother's request and files her upload.

cases.title: GP practice assistant sends the lab report the GP received
cases.why: Dr. Hofer knowingly addressed the assistant (register warning acknowledged). She is the named person; the author is Dr. Brandl, the requester on the report is the GP. FILE with clear Provenance; HOLD acceptable.

cases.title: New lab physician not in the register (Labor Westbahnhof)
cases.why: A new outside lab with its own labels, units (Tsd/µl, sek), other LOINC variants (34714-6, 3173-2, 26515-7) and a lab flag.

cases.title: Rehab colleague 'Andrea Moser' opens Stefan Kern's SMS link
cases.why: M2 on the SMS channel.

cases.title: The report's author Dr. Johanna Leitner opens Stefan Kern's link
cases.why: Clinically she is more authoritative, but the brief is explicit: the request is for the named person, a colleague may not answer.

cases.title: eID 'Stefan Johann Kern' for 'Stefan Kern'
cases.why: Extra given name in the eID.

cases.title: Retry: Dr. Brandl first uploads Max's report, then Maria's
cases.why: The sender corrects her own mistake. The link must stay usable after a wrong-patient block.
steps: upload lab-result-max-beispiel.md -> expect BLOCK + alert without Max's name
same session, upload lab-result-maria-beispiel.md -> expect FILE
check HAPI: exactly one DiagnosticReport for this Task, no Max data anywhere

cases.title: Rehab report says 'Übermittelt von: S. Kern'
cases.why: An initial for the verified sender's given name.

cases.title: Typo in the local part: 'eva.brand1@labor-kanal.example' (digit 1); someone else answers
cases.why: M1 moved to the local part. The domain is known so a domain-only look-alike check stays silent; the eID gate must still stop it. A pre-send warning is a bonus.
steps: create request -> record whether the card warns before sending
login as Erwin Brandner -> expect DENY

cases.title: SMS number with transposed digits '+43 660 000 0110'; stranger answers
cases.why: M1 on the SMS channel.

cases.title: German discharge report from Reha Waldblick
cases.why: Same report in German with Austrian terms.

cases.title: Stefan Kern uploads an older report from a DIFFERENT clinic (Reha Seeblick, 2024)
cases.why: Right patient, but neither the addressed clinic nor the requested stay: the answer to 'the rehab discharge report' after the hip replacement is not a 2024 knee rehab from another clinic. Filing it as the answer closes the Task with the wrong document.

cases.title: Interim report ('Zwischenbericht'), patient still in rehab
cases.why: Not a discharge report. Filing it as LOINC 11490-0 (discharge summary) and closing the Task is wrong.

cases.title: Discharge report with an embedded lab table
cases.why: Discharge letters often include labs. File as DocumentReference with the text; extracting Observations is optional.

cases.title: Recommendations list with a 'Patient:' bullet
cases.why: 'Patient:' here addresses the patient in a to-do list, it is not a second patient line.

cases.title: Kind mismatch: Stefan Kern uploads the rehab's discharge LAB report on the rehab request
cases.why: Correct patient and sender, wrong document kind for the request.

cases.title: Kind mismatch: Dr. Brandl uploads the rehab report on the lab request
cases.why: Right patient, wrong kind, and 'Sent by: Stefan Kern' contradicts the eID.

cases.title: Rehab report for another Maria Beispiel (b. 1958, also hip replacement)
cases.why: Same name, same story, different DOB.

cases.title: New rehab clinic (Reha Seeblick) asked directly; German report
cases.why: A legitimate answer from a clinic the network has never seen, with H3 sections, bold labels and a footer.

cases.title: 'Arztbrief' without a Stay line; 'Pat.: Beispiel, Maria, *12.03.1961'
cases.why: Rehab clinics call the discharge report 'Arztbrief'. 'Pat.' and '*' are standard abbreviations.
